content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Identify the main nutrients required by humans
Describe the functions of carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids
Describe the roles of vitamins and minerals
Explain why fibre and water are important in the diet

are substances obtained from food that the body needs for energy, growth, repair, and maintaining health. Humans require a variety of nutrients, each with specific functions. A healthy diet provides all essential nutrients in appropriate amounts.
Excess stored as glycogen or fat
Can be used for energy (17 kJ/g)
Energy source (39 kJ/g - more than carbs)
Saturated fats: linked to heart disease
A, D, E, K (stored in body)
Lipids provide more than twice the energy per gram as carbohydrates or proteins.
All fats are bad for you
Unsaturated fats are essential and beneficial
Excess of ANY energy source causes weight gain
Vitamins help release energy but don't provide it

A balanced diet usually provides all needed nutrients

Disease caused by lack of a nutrient
Amino acid that must come from diet
Seven nutrient types: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water
Carbohydrates provide main energy source (17 kJ/g)
Proteins needed for growth and repair
Lipids store energy (39 kJ/g) and insulate
Vitamins and minerals needed in small amounts for specific functions
Fibre aids digestion and prevents constipation
Water is essential for all body processes
Deficiency diseases result from lack of specific nutrients
